virals.text:
The old proverb says: “Don't give someone a fish, teach them to catch one.”

🎬 THE CHANCE HE NEVER FORGOT

A struggling street vendor. A young woman. A forgotten moment. And an unexpected act of kindness.

A 69-second cinematic AI short film about dignity, opportunity, and the power of kindness.

Want to create something similar? Here's the complete AI video prompt. 👇

---

🎥 THE COMPLETE VIDEO GENERATION PROMPT

Create a 69-second vertical (9:16, 1080x1920, 30fps) cinematic short film titled "The Chance He Never Forgot."

Tone: Intimate, warm, slightly melancholic, with a quiet twist of kindness.

Visual style: Shallow depth of field, handheld close-ups, warm street-lamp tones against cool winter light, soft snow in some scenes, and natural skin tones.

SCENE 1 (0–10s):
Extreme close-up of weathered hands counting folded dollar bills, establishing scarcity and care.

SCENE 2 (10–25s):
An older street vendor (gray beard, dark beanie, worn wool coat) sells small green Statue of Liberty figurines from a cardboard table on a city sidewalk. A young woman (dark wavy hair, dark coat) stops to look. Their exchange is subtle and unspoken.

SCENE 3 (25–40s):
Winter dusk. The vendor arranges figurines and snow-dusted glass globes on a wooden shelf. Camera slowly pushes in on his face.

SCENE 4 (40–55s):
Daytime. The woman walks past a "New York Souvenir Shop" storefront with red lettering, then pauses at the window.

SCENE 5 (55–69s):
Interior of a warm shop with green figurines on wooden shelves. The woman and an older man in a light blue shirt share a moment as he presses money into her hand. Hold on her expression: surprise, then gratitude. End on a slow fade to black with the title card.

AUDIO: Ambient city sound, soft piano, no dialogue unless specified.

PACING: Slow cuts, 2–4 seconds per shot.

AVOID: Real identifiable public figures, on-screen text other than the title card, and any reference to a real brand.

OUTPUT: One continuous shot list with timing, camera direction, lighting, and sound cues for each beat.

---

Sometimes, one small act of kindness becomes someone's unforgettable story. ❤️

What would you have done in the vendor's place?

virals.text:
SHOT OF THE DEAD is officially out.

It's a previs tool that runs in your browser. And it's finally here: you can build locations just by talking to your AI (MCP).

Ask Claude or ChatGPT for "a carousel at a night amusement park" and you get a 3D set you can actually shoot in. Drop a camera, pick the lens and the move, shoot. Then use those shots as the reference for your AI video. Way less rerolling.

Works for live action too. Ask for a tiny 9x9 ft room and you get something close to the real size, so you can figure out camera spots and lenses before you even get to the location.

A few things it does (just some of them):
- Build and edit locations by talking to your AI (MCP)
- Opens in the browser. No Blender, no Unreal
- Dolly zoom, 360 orbit, reverse shots across the 180 line, all quick
- Preset the focal lengths you use most (24mm, 35mm, 85mm...)
- Every shot lands in the Cut List so you can see the whole film
- Bring in 3D from Marble and others as a location (no limit on Pro)
- Export the input pack each AI video model needs: Seedance, Kling, Veo, Runway, MiniMax (Pro)
- No watermark, unlimited projects (Pro)

The Cut List is kind of the hidden gem. It's like pinning your storyboards on a wall. Drag shots around to check the flow. Each shot keeps its camera, lens and actor positions, so you can jump back into scene 5 or scene 98 and reshoot. Export everything as one MP4 or one file per shot, drop it into DaVinci Resolve and cut your previs.

Most of it is free. Link in the reply.

virals.text:
If your app still calls grok-imagine-image-pro or grok-imagine-image-quality, starting Nov 2 it gets grok-imagine-image-2.0 at quality "low". No error, no code change needed.

xAI retires grok-imagine-image-quality that day, but the slug keeps resolving. grok-imagine-image-pro has redirected to it since May 15, so pro ends up on 2.0 at low too. Same request and response shape, and xAI says low is $0.01 per image cheaper.

Low may be fine for you. xAI says it ranks #2 on Arena's image-edit leaderboard. But the redirect picks your tier, and the obvious fix picks a different one. Change the model string to grok-imagine-image-2.0 without a quality field and you get auto. Auto serves low for generations and medium for edits, billed at whatever was served. So the one-line migration and the redirect disagree on edits.

🎬 THE CHANCE HE NEVER FORGOT

A struggling street vendor. A young woman. A forgotten moment. And an unexpected act of kindness.

A 69-second cinematic AI short film about dignity, opportunity, and the power of kindness.

Want to create something similar? Here's the complete AI video prompt. 👇

---

🎥 THE COMPLETE VIDEO GENERATION PROMPT

Create a 69-second vertical (9:16, 1080x1920, 30fps) cinematic short film titled "The Chance He Never Forgot."

Tone: Intimate, warm, slightly melancholic, with a quiet twist of kindness.

Visual style: Shallow depth of field, handheld close-ups, warm street-lamp tones against cool winter light, soft snow in some scenes, and natural skin tones.

SCENE 1 (0–10s):
Extreme close-up of weathered hands counting folded dollar bills, establishing scarcity and care.

SCENE 2 (10–25s):
An older street vendor (gray beard, dark beanie, worn wool coat) sells small green Statue of Liberty figurines from a cardboard table on a city sidewalk. A young woman (dark wavy hair, dark coat) stops to look. Their exchange is subtle and unspoken.

SCENE 3 (25–40s):
Winter dusk. The vendor arranges figurines and snow-dusted glass globes on a wooden shelf. Camera slowly pushes in on his face.

SCENE 4 (40–55s):
Daytime. The woman walks past a "New York Souvenir Shop" storefront with red lettering, then pauses at the window.

SCENE 5 (55–69s):
Interior of a warm shop with green figurines on wooden shelves. The woman and an older man in a light blue shirt share a moment as he presses money into her hand. Hold on her expression: surprise, then gratitude. End on a slow fade to black with the title card.

AUDIO: Ambient city sound, soft piano, no dialogue unless specified.

PACING: Slow cuts, 2–4 seconds per shot.

AVOID: Real identifiable public figures, on-screen text other than the title card, and any reference to a real brand.

OUTPUT: One continuous shot list with timing, camera direction, lighting, and sound cues for each beat.

---

Sometimes, one small act of kindness becomes someone's unforgettable story. ❤️

What would you have done in the vendor's place?

outsiders.text:
SHOT OF THE DEAD is officially out.

It's a previs tool that runs in your browser. And it's finally here: you can build locations just by talking to your AI (MCP).

Ask Claude or ChatGPT for "a carousel at a night amusement park" and you get a 3D set you can actually shoot in. Drop a camera, pick the lens and the move, shoot. Then use those shots as the reference for your AI video. Way less rerolling.

Works for live action too. Ask for a tiny 9x9 ft room and you get something close to the real size, so you can figure out camera spots and lenses before you even get to the location.

A few things it does (just some of them):
- Build and edit locations by talking to your AI (MCP)
- Opens in the browser. No Blender, no Unreal
- Dolly zoom, 360 orbit, reverse shots across the 180 line, all quick
- Preset the focal lengths you use most (24mm, 35mm, 85mm...)
- Every shot lands in the Cut List so you can see the whole film
- Bring in 3D from Marble and others as a location (no limit on Pro)
- Export the input pack each AI video model needs: Seedance, Kling, Veo, Runway, MiniMax (Pro)
- No watermark, unlimited projects (Pro)

The Cut List is kind of the hidden gem. It's like pinning your storyboards on a wall. Drag shots around to check the flow. Each shot keeps its camera, lens and actor positions, so you can jump back into scene 5 or scene 98 and reshoot. Export everything as one MP4 or one file per shot, drop it into DaVinci Resolve and cut your previs.

Most of it is free. Link in the reply.

outsiders.text:
If your app still calls grok-imagine-image-pro or grok-imagine-image-quality, starting Nov 2 it gets grok-imagine-image-2.0 at quality "low". No error, no code change needed.

xAI retires grok-imagine-image-quality that day, but the slug keeps resolving. grok-imagine-image-pro has redirected to it since May 15, so pro ends up on 2.0 at low too. Same request and response shape, and xAI says low is $0.01 per image cheaper.

Low may be fine for you. xAI says it ranks #2 on Arena's image-edit leaderboard. But the redirect picks your tier, and the obvious fix picks a different one. Change the model string to grok-imagine-image-2.0 without a quality field and you get auto. Auto serves low for generations and medium for edits, billed at whatever was served. So the one-line migration and the redirect disagree on edits.

Before Nov 2:
1. Find the old slugs: grep -rnE 'grok-imagine-image-(pro|quality)' .
2. Send model and quality together on every call. Pick low or medium for generations and edits separately.
3. After the switch, log the model field on responses. xAI says it reports the model that actually served the request.

grok-imagine-image (1.0) isn't affected.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
